article.title: NFL EDGE Tuesday Morning Brief
article.dek: Week 10 is over — the Chargers finally won, the Ravens lost a fifth straight, and the board hasn't flipped to Week 11 yet, so today is a settle-and-wait day.

items.headline: Lead: The Chargers finally won — 23-20 over the Ravens on Monday night
paragraphs: The Los Angeles Chargers beat the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night Football. It is their first win of the season. They are 1-8. Baltimore lost its fifth straight and fell to 4-6.

Justin Herbert ran for a first-quarter touchdown and Omarion Hampton ran for 105 yards and a score. The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160-16. Derrick Henry was held to 10 yards on 10 carries, though he scored twice.
Jacoby Brissett threw for 340 yards in his Ravens debut. But a Zay Flowers fumble with 2:03 left ended Baltimore's last real drive, and the Hail Mary at the end fell short.
The 43 combined points went over the 39.5 closing total. The Chargers covered as 4.5-point underdogs.
items.takeaway: Week 10 is done. The Chargers finally won, the Ravens lost a fifth straight, and the total went over the 39.5 close.

items.headline: No games today, and the board hasn't flipped to Week 11 yet
paragraphs: There are no NFL games today. The next games come Thursday night.
The app's board is still on Week 10 and still lists last night's game — with the books having pulled its lines after the final, so there is nothing to price.
All three headline cards are empty. Hit Rate, Balanced, and Value all say no play. That is the board telling you there is nothing to do today.
items.takeaway: No games, no cards, no lines to check. Today is a settle-and-wait day until the board flips to Week 11.

items.headline: Injury check: no new injuries out of Monday night
paragraphs: No injury news came out of Monday night's game in the overnight recaps.
Lamar Jackson is still out for Baltimore. Jacoby Brissett started in his place and threw for 340 yards in his debut.
Thursday's inactive lists come out about 90 minutes before kickoff. That is the next injury news that matters — check the board Thursday and read the lists before you play anything.
items.takeaway: No new injuries to track. Jackson is still out, Brissett is the starter until that changes, and Thursday's inactives are the next thing to watch.

items.headline: Last night's Hit Rate pick lost — log it, and look at what the app got right
paragraphs: The evening brief's only card was Hit Rate on Baltimore moneyline at -225. Baltimore lost 23-20. If you played it, that is a loss. Log it.
The loss doesn't mean the app misread the game. The app had the game about even — its expected margin was roughly -0.12 — and it projected about 44 points against a 39.5 total. The real total was 43.

Hit Rate is the card that forgoes value for win probability. A -225 favorite losing is exactly why the price still matters, and why the app shows you the play-through: -225 was inside it, but inside the line is not a guarantee.
items.takeaway: Log the loser. The app read the game close to right — nearly even, nearly 44 points — and the favorite still lost. That is football, and that is why settlement has to be honest.

items.headline: No cards today means no forcing it
paragraphs: All three cards are empty today. That is not a broken board — it is a board with nothing to price, because Week 10 is over and Week 11 hasn't posted yet.
When the board flips to Week 11, the cards come back with it. Check the board then and let the app tell you what, if anything, is worth a look.
items.takeaway: An empty board is an answer, not a problem. Wait for the Week 11 flip — don't go hunting for a bet the app hasn't priced.

items.headline: Learn the Game: a push — when nobody wins and you get your money back
paragraphs: A push is a bet that lands exactly on the number. Say, as a clearly labeled hypothetical, you bet a team -3 and they win by exactly 3. Nobody wins that bet. Your stake comes back.
The same thing happens with totals. As a clearly labeled hypothetical, you bet over 44 and the game finishes with 44 total points. That is a push too — stake back, no win, no loss.
Books usually list a push as a refund, not a win or a loss. It doesn't help or hurt your record. It just hands your money back.
items.takeaway: A push is a tie with the number: your stake comes back, no win, no loss. It is the one outcome where the book and the bettor both walk away even.

items.headline: Nothing moved overnight — the lines are pulled and Week 11 hasn't posted
paragraphs: There is no line movement to report this morning. The books pulled the lines on Chargers-Ravens after the final, and the Week 11 lines haven't posted to the board yet.

For the record, the closing numbers held from the evening: the spread closed at Ravens -4.5 and the Chargers covered; the total closed at 39.5 and finished at 43, so the over hit. The app had flagged the total's move from 38.5 to 39.5 in the evening brief, and it projected about 44 points.
When the Week 11 board posts, the movement that matters starts there — openers against where the lines settle. Check the board when it flips.
items.takeaway: No movement overnight: last night's lines are gone and Week 11 hasn't posted. The closer tells the story — Chargers covered, the total went over.

items.headline: Today's job: settle last night honestly, then wait for Thursday
paragraphs: If you played anything on Monday night, settle it now while the result is fresh. Baltimore moneyline -225 lost. The total over 39.5 won. The Chargers +4.5 covered.
Settlement is manual — the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
Then wait. There is nothing to play today, and a good number Thursday beats a forced bet Tuesday. Check the board when it flips to Week 11.
items.takeaway: Settle Monday night now, log the losers too, and wait for the Week 11 board. Nothing today is worth forcing.
